stories.body: Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin are due to hold their first trilateral meeting on the sidelines of the APEC summit in Shenzhen. The White House says Trump plans to discuss the war with Iran and a possible nuclear arms agreement; Ukraine is not expected to be on the formal agenda. The talks have prompted concerns about deals over spheres of influence, although analysts caution that the leaders have competing objectives and few concrete outcomes are expected. Trump and Xi also face unresolved trade and technology disputes following their 2025 tariff truce.
stories.headline: Trump, Xi and Putin prepare for first three-way summit in Shenzhen

stories.body: The International Court of Justice is due to deliver judgment Thursday in The Gambia’s case accusing Myanmar of genocide against the Rohingya. The case concerns a 2017 military campaign that drove at least 730,000 people into Bangladesh, with survivors describing killings, mass rape and village burnings. Myanmar denies genocide and disputes evidence of intent to destroy the group. A finding that Myanmar committed genocide would be unprecedented for the court and could influence other cases. The judgment will be binding, but enforcement options are limited; the ICJ determines state responsibility rather than prosecuting individuals.
stories.headline: UN court to rule on Myanmar’s responsibility for alleged Rohingya genocide

stories.body: Israeli forces advanced beyond the Yellow Line into central Gaza on Wednesday, sending displaced Palestinians fleeing shelters near Nuseirat and closing part of the main north-south road. Israel said the operation targeted a tunnel posing an immediate threat to its troops; Hamas called the incursion a violation of the October 2025 ceasefire. Witnesses reported artillery fire and airstrikes, while Palestinian medics reported deaths. The advance followed a warning from the body overseeing the ceasefire that both sides were failing to meet their commitments, with continuing violence and dire living conditions threatening the agreement.
stories.headline: Israeli tanks cross Gaza ceasefire boundary, forcing residents to flee

stories.body: The Saudi-led coalition says it struck 60 Houthi military targets in Yemen as the rebels advanced toward Aden, the temporary capital of the internationally recognised government. Government-aligned forces withdrew from territory near the Bab al-Mandeb shipping chokepoint to reinforce the city. Fighting also intensified around Taiz, where local authorities accuse the Houthis of shelling residential areas and obstructing medicine deliveries. The coalition said it intercepted two cruise missiles aimed at Riyadh; the Houthis claimed attacks on Saudi oil and military infrastructure.
stories.headline: Saudi-led coalition strikes Houthi targets as rebels advance toward Aden

stories.body: Pete Hegseth made an unannounced visit to Caracas on Wednesday, announcing renewed military cooperation and meeting acting president Delcy Rodríguez. The visit underscored the rapprochement since US forces seized Nicolás Maduro in January, after which Rodríguez took power with Washington’s support. Hegseth praised the operation that captured Maduro and said the countries would deepen defence and economic ties, including developing Venezuela’s resources. Maduro remains imprisoned in New York while his former allies continue to govern.
stories.headline: Hegseth visits Caracas to renew US military cooperation with Venezuela

stories.body: A UN Population Fund report says one in four women globally cannot refuse sex when their husband or partner demands it. The reported proportion reaches 45% in west and central Africa, compared with 33% in east and southern Africa and Arab states, and 10% in Latin America and the Caribbean. Analysis of eight countries with comparable data found girls and women aged 15–19 had less power to refuse than those aged 45–49. Rights advocates called for stronger protection against marital rape, highlighting laws that exempt husbands from prosecution and leave married children especially vulnerable.
stories.headline: UN report says one in four women cannot refuse sex with a partner

stories.body: Vanuatu’s environment minister, Ralph Regenvanu, called for changes to the UN climate summit process, accusing a small group of countries of blocking progress. He warned that COP31 risks reversing earlier commitments rather than strengthening climate action.
stories.headline: Vanuatu urges climate summit reform, warning COP31 could weaken commitments

stories.body: Anthropic says the company and its co-founders sold 980 million shares at $83 each, raising $81.3 billion ahead of Thursday’s Nasdaq debut under the ticker ANT. A separate $26 billion private placement brings the combined fundraising to $107.3 billion. Strong demand pushed the offering above its initial price range, valuing the Claude developer at roughly $1.5 trillion. The listing will test investor confidence in AI providers as chip and data-centre stocks retreat. Anthropic has reported rapid revenue growth, driven partly by Claude Code, but questions remain about whether future profits can justify its valuation.
stories.headline: Anthropic prices shares at $83 ahead of closely watched Nasdaq debut

stories.body: House Democrats nominated Hakeem Jeffries for speaker in a 251–11 caucus vote, putting him on course to become the first Black person to lead the chamber when the new Congress convenes on January 3. Democrats have secured at least 257 House seats and also won Senate control. Progressive holdouts sought commitments on healthcare, immigration enforcement, campaign finance and military aid to Israel. Jeffries pledged to tackle living costs and healthcare affordability, but delivering legislation will require managing internal divisions and confronting Trump’s veto power.
stories.headline: Democrats nominate Jeffries for House speaker after sweeping midterm gains

stories.body: Moderate Democrats are exploring an immigration deal with Trump after the midterms, seeking legal pathways for some undocumented immigrants alongside border security and limits on ICE enforcement. Henry Cuellar has contacted immigration officials, while incoming senators James Talarico and Annie Andrews have expressed interest in negotiations. Trump’s recent openness to some legal pathways has encouraged them, but Stephen Miller’s promotion to chief of staff and opposition within both parties remain major obstacles. Republican governor Kevin Stitt also urged reform, proposing state-issued workforce permits backed by employers. No agreement has been reached.
stories.headline: Democrats seek immigration talks with Trump despite Miller’s promotion

stories.body: Minutes from the Federal Reserve’s October meeting opened with an unusual warning about debt linked to the AI boom. Officials raised concerns that a reversal could threaten financial stability, adding to doubts spreading on Wall Street about the sector’s expansion.
stories.headline: Federal Reserve flags financial risks from AI-related debt

stories.body: Pedro Sánchez and Alberto Núñez Feijóo face a 90-minute debate Thursday as the PSOE seeks to close a roughly two-point gap with the PP ahead of the November 29 election. Polling suggests a substantially wider advantage for the combined right over the left, excluding nationalist parties, with more undecided voters on the left. Sánchez’s team says he has studied his difficulties in their 2023 encounter. Feijóo plans an aggressive challenge while maintaining a presidential image. Both campaigns see mobilising their own potential voters as central to the debate’s impact.
stories.headline: Sánchez and Feijóo prepare for pivotal debate before November 29 election

stories.body: Congress’s standing committee ratified seven government decrees covering dependency care, protection for single-parent and large families, railway safety, and assistance following the Urda train crash, flooding and Ceuta’s migration emergency. The PP supported all seven despite criticising their timing; Vox backed only the train-crash assistance decree, while Junts abstained on single-parent protections. Opposition parties accused the government of using emergency legislation to promote its record with parliament dissolved and the election approaching. Ministers argued that the measures were urgent and should not wait for the next legislature.
stories.headline: Congress ratifies seven social decrees amid electioneering accusations

stories.body: Spain has committed at COP31 to developing a national fossil-fuel phaseout roadmap. According to sources familiar with the government’s text, it targets 100% renewable electricity by 2040 and a fully decarbonised economy without oil, gas or coal by 2050. Interim goals include 81% renewable electricity and 48% renewable energy in final consumption by 2030. The strategy emphasises efficiency, electrification and renewable generation, prioritising buildings, services, agriculture and urban transport before extending the transition to harder-to-electrify industry and heavy transport.
stories.headline: Spain outlines roadmap for fully renewable electricity by 2040

stories.body: Barcelona approved 75-year development rights on five municipal plots for Habitatge Metròpolis Barcelona to build 410 permanently protected rental homes in Sant Martí and Sants-Montjuïc. The city will retain ownership of the land. Construction is expected to begin on Ferrocarrils Catalans before the end of 2026, on three further developments in early 2027, and on Tànger in early 2028. The public-private operator is also studying another 528 homes. Councillors broadly supported the project, although Barcelona en Comú criticised delays in delivering earlier developments.
stories.headline: Barcelona approves five municipal plots for 410 affordable rental homes

stories.body: An agreement between the PSC and Barcelona en Comú, also backed by ERC, secured provisional approval for a revised redevelopment plan around the Sants railway deck and Rambla de Badal. It reduces the number of homes affected by the longstanding scheme from nearly 700 to 12 and preserves the building at Rambla de Badal 188. A proposed 50-home public development on Riera de Tena would rehouse the 12 affected families and add public housing. The agreement also provides conservation and rehabilitation measures for 26 properties. The plan still requires approval by the full council.
stories.headline: Sants redevelopment advances with plans to protect existing homes and build 50 more

stories.body: Barcelona approved an additional €5.73 million for the Rambla renovation, citing more extensive archaeological work, extra security bollards, metro-station waterproofing, sewer repairs and heritage improvements. The revised construction budget is approximately €42.9 million. City officials said the changes reflect conditions discovered during the works and later security requirements. Completion remains scheduled for February 2027, with an inauguration planned for February 13–14. The redesign widens pedestrian areas, creates three squares and reduces traffic to one lane in each direction, primarily for residents, services and public transport.
stories.headline: Rambla renovation costs rise by €5.7 million

stories.body: Barcelona’s Thursday forecast calls for brief, locally intense showers before dawn and strong winds through midday, with gusts exceeding 60 km/h in coastal and nearby inland areas and potentially topping 70 km/h in some places. Meteocat’s wind warning runs until 1 p.m. Mild early temperatures are expected to fall through the day as winds ease toward evening. Friday and the weekend should feel cooler, particularly overnight, with some wind continuing Friday.
stories.headline: Strong winds forecast for Barcelona before a cooler weekend
